entries.name: Ecuadorian Independence Day
entries.capsule: Ecuador's national day, marking Quito's 1809 call for independence; Minnesota families often celebrate on a nearby Sunday.
entries.dateRule: August 10 each year. Minnesota community celebrations are often moved to a nearby Sunday.

dates.source: Fixed date, Aug. 10, stated by Teleamazonas (a 2026 article; Ecuador can move holidays to a nearby weekday by law, so later years are not confirmed)
Fixed date, Aug. 10, stated by Teleamazonas (a 2026 article; Ecuador can move holidays to a nearby weekday by law, so later years are not confirmed)

entries.whatItMarks: The August 10, 1809 call for independence from Spain in Quito, known as the Primer Grito de Independencia.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Families hold outdoor celebrations with music, folk dance, food and ecuavoley on a Sunday near Aug. 10. In 2017 the dance group Indi Samay performed in a restaurant parking lot at 40th and Central in Columbia Heights; organizers chose Sunday because Aug. 10 fell on a workday. In 2026, EcuaFiesta was held Aug. 2 at Los Andes Latin Bistro in Northeast Minneapolis (see its own entry).

entries.name: EcuaFiesta (Minneapolis)
entries.capsule: Free Northeast Minneapolis festival of Ecuadorian independence: music, folk dance, ecuavoley tournament, food and vendors.
entries.dateRule: Announced each year by organizers; held on a Sunday near Aug. 10 in 2026.
entries.whatItMarks: Ecuadorian independence and community, celebrated as a family festival.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In 2026, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. at Los Andes Latin Bistro, 2300 University Ave. NE, with live music, folkloric dance, an ecuavoley tournament, Ecuadorian food, local vendors and family activities. The organizer is not named in the listing.

entries.name: Feast of the Virgen del Cisne
entries.capsule: Marian feast from southern Ecuador; a Minneapolis parish has held a Mass, robe-changing and street procession in mid-August.
entries.dateRule: Around August 15, with community celebrations often on the nearest weekend. Set by each parish.
entries.whatItMarks: Devotion to a statue of the Virgin Mary acquired more than four centuries ago by Indigenous people in El Cisne, Ecuador.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In 2010, Sagrado Corazon de Jesus in Minneapolis held a Mass on Aug. 15, changed the statue's robe, led a three-block procession, and continued with music, dance and Ecuadorian food after a day of games in a nearby park on Aug. 14. No later Minnesota celebration was confirmed.

entries.name: Ss. Cyril and Methodius Church Festival
entries.capsule: Northeast Minneapolis parish festival with Ecuadorian food, soccer and volleyball tournaments, dance and raffle, usually an August weekend.
entries.dateRule: Announced each year by the parish; recent years fell on a Saturday (sometimes with Sunday) in mid- to late August.
entries.whatItMarks: Annual parish fundraiser and gathering at a church that has been predominantly Hispanic, with many Ecuadorian members, since 1997.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Saturday soccer and volleyball tournaments, Ecuadorian food, kids' games, beer wagon, ice cream and raffle; in 2019 also traditional dance and Sunday Masses in English and Spanish.

entries.name: Hispanic Heritage Month (begins)
entries.capsule: U.S. heritage month, Sept. 15 to Oct. 15. In 2026 a Minneapolis dance festival featured Ecuador during the month.
entries.whatItMarks: U.S. recognition of Hispanic and Latino Americans, timed to several Latin American independence days.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: No Ecuadorian-specific Heritage Month event was found. The Minnesota International Dance Festival, which overlapped the month in 2026, chose Ecuador as guest country (see its own entry).
